text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.
White sugar futures in London closed mixed in quiet dealings. Front month May lost 50 cents to close at $317.90 per tonne, while October added 50 cents to close at $308.00 per tonne.

Raw sugar futures in New York ended weaker but off the lows in thin dealings. July lost 6 points to close at 11.05 cents/lb while October gave up 5 points to close at 10.85 cents/lb. Some analysts still expect prices to come under pressure once the July contract is off the board.

The Brazilian government will publish on Thursday authorization for exporters to start shipping sugar set aside in the government crop plan with a zero export tax, official sources said. The publication of the notice is necessary to exempt exporters from a 40 per cent export tax which otherwise applies to sugars exported in excess of the 5.39 million tonnes set aside for export in the 1997/98 (May/April) crop plan.

Despite expectations of a higher sugar cane crop the export target is only slightly above that of last year as the government intends to use the extra sugar cane production to increase alcohol output.

RUSSIA - Sugar imports into Russia continued to gather pace in March. Total imports in March 1997 amounted to 199,000 tonnes, tel quel, after 113,000 tonnes in February and 91,000 tonnes in January. This brought cumulative imports in the first quarter of 1997 up to 424,491 tonnes, raw value, which is still sharply down on the 1.083 million tonnes imported in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1996 reached 3.236 million tonnes against 3.186 million tonnes in 1995.

Ukraine continues to be the largest supplier of white sugar, delivering a total of 210,600 tonnes in January/March 1997, down from 378,801 tonnes in 1996. Cuba is dominating raw sugar supplies, shipping a total of 94,400 tonnes against 344,400 tonnes in 1996. Other important suppliers in 1997 were Brazil (28,500 tonnes raws vs 161,600 tonnes) and Moldova (23,000 tonnes whites vs 19,700 tonnes). Given rising prices on the Russian market, raw sugar imports can be expected to accelerate in the coming months.

UNITED KINGDOM - Sugar imports in February 1997 amounted to 108,076 tonnes, raw value, down from 119,229 tonnes in February 1996. This brought cumulative imports in the first 5 months of 1996/97 (October/February) up to 540,484 tonnes against 576,752 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995/96 reached 1.380 million tonnes against 1.635 million tonnes in 1994/95.

Major countries of origin in 1996/97 were Mauritius with 236,481 tonnes raws against 297,733 tonnes, Guyana with 101,643 tonnes, up from 65,310 tonnes, and Fiji with 79,900 tonnes, down from 85,180 tonnes. Sugar exports in February 1997 amounted to 27,345 tonnes compared to 24,661 tonnes in February 1996.

This brought cumulative exports in October/February 1996/97 up to 109,758 tonnes against 125,983 tonnes in 1995/96. Total exports in 1995/96 fell to 390,747 tonnes from 560,076 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in 1996/97 were Israel with 37,399 tonnes whites against 32,906 tonnes and Norway with 17,151 tonnes, down from 19,466 tonnes.

DENMARK - The weather in the week ended May 11 was rather changeable with cold temperatures and ample rainfall. Cumulative precipitation since April 1, 1997 ranged between 39-79 mm compared to the long term mean of 52-55 mm. Beets are in good condition and their development is considered to be satisfactory. Thrips attacks were reported from some growing regions. The overall crop outlook is normal.

The European Union awarded 70,100 tonnes of white sugar at a maximum refund of ECU 43.042 per 100 kg at its weekly tender on May 14. Cumulative awards so far made under the 1996/97 series of tenders for the period up to May 14 reached 1,996,100 tonnes, which compares to 2,103,948 tonnes last year.
